sections.h2: Where is the Warren County Register of Deeds and when is it open?
sections.html:
The Warren County Register of Deeds sits at 109 South Main Street in Warrenton, and the office posts hours of 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. The mailing address is P.O. Box 506, Warrenton, NC 27589, and the phone number printed on the office website is (252) 257-3265.

The register of deeds is an elected county office in North Carolina, chosen by the county's voters every two years under G.S. 161-1. If you need to find out who owns a Warren County parcel, the office says it can search only by owner name. Without a name, it points callers to the tax office instead.

Warren County describes itself as a council-manager county run by a five-member board of commissioners. The county was established in 1779, covers 443 square miles of rolling fields according to the county manager's page, and has roughly 20,000 residents. That small, rural footprint matters to a seller: the recording office is one counter, and a call ahead usually settles a question faster than a trip.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed in Warren County actually do?
sections.html:
Recording puts a deed on the public record, and in North Carolina that step decides who wins a priority dispute. Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance or lease over three years does not bind lien creditors or purchasers who paid value until it is registered in the county where the land lies. Priority follows the time of registration.

The Warren County office describes its job in plain terms: it lets the owner of an interest in property give public notice of that ownership. Everything it holds is open to the public. The staff also keeps vital records for births in Warren County, marriage licenses, and notary oaths, and it records military discharge papers (DD-214) at no charge to veterans.

  • Deeds, deeds of trust, satisfactions, plats and powers of attorney go on the land record.
  • Wills are not kept here. Probate matters belong to the clerk of superior court.
  • Liens and judgments are checked through the clerk of court, which the office's own FAQ lists at (252) 257-6300.

sections.h2: What are the recording fees for a deed in Warren County?
sections.html:
A general deed costs $26.00 for the first 15 pages plus $4.00 for every page after that, set statewide by G.S. 161-10. A deed of trust or mortgage costs $64.00 for the first 35 pages plus $4.00 per extra page. Satisfactions and cancellations of a deed of trust carry no fee.

The table below pulls the statute figures that apply to most home sales, along with items the Warren office lists on its own pages.

Warren County's own fee page and FAQ carry older wording, including a different charge per extra page and an old deeds of trust figure. Ask the register of deeds to confirm the total before you send a document, and use the statute as the baseline.

sections.h2: Who pays the excise tax on a Warren County deed?
sections.html:
The seller pays. G.S. 105-228.30 says the transferor must pay the tax to the register of deeds of the county where the land is, before the deed is recorded, at one dollar for each five hundred dollars or fractional part of the price or value.

The register collects it at the counter or through the closing attorney's recording package, and then splits it. Half goes to the county general fund and half is sent monthly to the state Department of Revenue, with a small allowance the county keeps. The rule is on the statute page.

Warren's older office FAQ states the same rate as $2.00 per $1,000. That is the same ratio written another way. Because the tax scales with the price, a seller should ask the closing attorney for the exact stamp figure on the settlement statement rather than estimating.

sections.h2: What should a Warren County seller check before the deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Confirm three things: the names on the deed match the title, the tax account is current, and the document meets the office's page standards. The office's checklist and fee pages are on the register's website, and the staff answers questions by phone.

  • Ask whether the deed needs a new document to add or remove a name. The office says changing names on a deed takes a new deed, drawn by an attorney, then recorded for the usual fee, plus excise tax if a price applies.
  • Check the property tax account at the county tax office, since county tax bills come due each year under G.S. 105-360 on September 1 and interest starts after January 5.
  • Ask whether any lien or judgment appears with the clerk of superior court.
  • Ask the register about payment forms. The office FAQ says it takes cash, check or money order, with no credit cards.

Sellers who skip the lien check are the ones who find a surprise at closing. A quick call to both the register and the tax office before listing costs nothing.

sections.h2: How does Warren County's rural setting affect a sale?
sections.html:
Warren County is a rural county of about 20,000 people, so a sale often involves acreage, a farm tract or a family parcel rather than a subdivision lot. Those transfers can involve a survey, a plat or an easement, and each has its own recording line.

Plats cost $21.00 per sheet under state law. If your sale includes a split of acreage, ask the register what a plat must look like before the surveyor finishes it. For tax maps, parcel numbers and aerial maps, the register's FAQ sends callers to the county tax mapping office at (252) 257-4158.

Owners who inherited a Warren County house and plan to sell should check whether the deed was ever recorded in the heirs' names. An unrecorded estate often needs the clerk's office first, then the register.

Map copies from the register are listed at five cents a page, with larger recorded maps at fifty cents a page, on the office FAQ. Deed copies in the office are listed at five cents a page, and scanned deeds can be viewed through the online search on the register's site.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Warren County house that has liens or repairs due?
sections.html:
Yes. Liens and unpaid taxes get paid from the sale proceeds at closing, and the closing attorney records the satisfactions. A house in poor condition can still sell as-is to a buyer who accepts it that way.

Do not wait on the record search. Get a title search early so the register's index and the clerk's judgment docket are both checked. If you want a straight answer on a cash sale in Warren County, you can request an offer from this site and compare it with a listing.

faqs.q: Does the Warren County Register of Deeds charge for recording a satisfaction of a deed of trust?
faqs.a: No. State law sets no fee for recording satisfactions or cancellations of deeds of trust or mortgages, and the Warren office lists cancellations as no fee.

faqs.q: Can the Warren County Register of Deeds tell me who owns a parcel by address?
faqs.a: Not by address. The office says it can search by owner name only, and it points callers without a name to the county tax office.

faqs.q: Are wills recorded at the Warren County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: No. Wills and estate matters go through the clerk of superior court. The register records deeds, deeds of trust, plats, satisfactions, marriage licenses and notary oaths.

faqs.q: Is there a fee for recording a military discharge in Warren County?
faqs.a: No. The Warren County Register of Deeds says it records DD-214 discharges free of charge for retired military.

faqs.q: Which county office do I call about a Warren County deed question?
faqs.a: Call the register of deeds at (252) 257-3265 during office hours of 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. The office is at 109 South Main Street in Warrenton.
